sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Warren, Ohio different?
sections.html:
Warren is the seat of Trumbull County, on the Mahoning River about 14 miles northwest of Youngstown and 56 miles southeast of Cleveland. Selling here means working with a city whose rules for rentals, vacant houses and contractors are written into its Codified Ordinances.

For mid-2025 the Census Bureau estimates 38,328 people, below the 39,201 counted in 2020 and the 41,557 counted in 2010. Whether you hold an inherited house, a rental or a vacant property, the sections below cover the local and county steps that apply.

sections.h2: How did Warren's industrial past shape its housing?
sections.html:
The town was founded in 1798 on land bought from the Connecticut Land Company and became the Trumbull County seat in 1801. By 1888 four railroads served it. Packard Electric and Packard Motor Car were both founded in Warren in the 1890s, and steel became a major industry across the county through the 20th century. The Trumbull Steel mill, later part of Republic Steel, kept running under various owners until 2012.

Population followed the mills. Warren peaked at 63,494 in 1970 and has fallen in every census since, to 46,832 in 2000 and 39,201 in 2020. Many late 19th and early 20th century buildings still stand around Courthouse Square. The larger employers now include St. Joseph Warren Hospital, the Tribune Chronicle and Thomas Steel Strip, and Kimberly-Clark announced plans in 2024 for a new paper production facility in the city.

sections.h2: What does it cost to own a home in Warren?
sections.html:
The Census survey covering 2020 through 2024 describes a city of low values and many renters.

  • Owners occupy 56.1% of housing units.
  • The middle owner-occupied house is valued at $86,400.
  • Owners pay $967 a month with a mortgage and $409 without one.
  • Gross rent at the midpoint is $766.
  • There are 16,871 households with 2.16 people each.
  • Household income at the midpoint is $37,887, and 31.9% of residents live in poverty.

At these values a repair bill can equal a large part of the price, so buyers weigh condition closely and expect the seller to say what is wrong.

sections.h2: Does a rental in Warren need a dwelling permit?
sections.html:
Yes. Under section 1367.10 of Warren's Codified Ordinances, no dwelling unit that lacks at least one owner living in it can be occupied without a residential non-owner occupied dwelling permit from the Health Officer's office. The permit is issued after a Building Inspector confirms compliance with the Housing, Building, Zoning and fire codes.

  • The annual fee for a single-unit dwelling is $120, and multi-unit buildings pay $100 per unit for two to fifty units, with lower per-unit rates above that.
  • A permit lasts one year and cannot be transferred to a new owner, so whoever buys a tenant-occupied house applies in their own name.
  • The Water Department will not open service for a non-owner-occupied unit without proof of the permit.
  • Occupying a unit without a permit carries a $1,000 fine, and each day counts as a separate violation.

Before listing a rental, ask the Health Department whether the permit is current, and tell the buyer it does not travel with the deed.

sections.h2: When does an empty Warren house count as vacant?
sections.html:
Chapter 1338 sets up a Vacant Property Registry. An owner has 30 days after a structure becomes vacant to register it with the Code Official. The annual fee is $200 for a residential structure, though it can be avoided if the property is secured, free of trash, mowed, and shows a visible address. Missing the filing deadline costs $50 per day up to $1,000.

One rule bears directly on a sale. A house under a signed broker listing agreement is not counted as vacant during the first six months of that listing, while an empty house offered for sale by its owner counts as vacant immediately. If you have moved out and plan to sell without a broker, register or secure the property first.

sections.h2: Do you need a contractor to fix up a Warren house before selling?
sections.html:
Not always. Chapter 1305 makes contractors register with the city, posting a $25,000 surety bond and showing insurance, yet it exempts a homeowner working on the single-family house they live in. That owner files a waiver of liability with the Building Division, and permits under Chapter 1307 still apply.

A hired contractor must hold the registration first, and one who starts without it pays double the fee. Ask any contractor for the city registration before work begins.

sections.h2: How does the Trumbull County Board of Revision work?
sections.html:
Three county offices, the Auditor, the Treasurer and the Commissioners, or their representatives, make up the Board of Revision. It rules on value complaints, homestead and owner-occupancy disputes and some penalty remission requests, and it leaves the tax dollars on your bill alone. Whoever files carries the burden of proof.

  • Complaints go to the Trumbull County Auditor, who acts as the board's secretary, by email at BOR@co.trumbull.oh.us, mail, fax or in person. A handwritten form needs a notary, and a form completed on a computer and emailed does not.
  • Useful evidence includes an independent appraisal, photos, repair estimates and, after a recent sale, the settlement statement and purchase agreement.
  • Hearings can be attended in person, by phone or on video, with at least ten days of notice.
  • Disagree with the outcome and you have 30 days from the decision letter to appeal to the state tax appeals board or the county court.

The window under Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 closes at the end of March following the tax year. An outside party can seek a higher value only when a recent arm's length sale beat the listed value by ten percent and by a state threshold, which the county page sets at $567,000 for tax year 2025.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks stay with the owner in Trumbull County?
sections.html:
The county's Homestead Exemption serves owners who are 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or a surviving spouse who was at least 59 when the exemption holder died. It shields up to $29,000 of market value, and the income cap for 2026 taxes payable in 2027 is $41,000 of Ohio adjusted gross income. Veterans who are 100% permanently disabled from service may receive up to $58,000 with no income cap.

Owner Occupancy gives a reduction of about 2.5% to those who live in the home, on one acre and the house. Both follow the owner who lives in the home, so a buyer starts without them.

sections.h2: What does Ohio require when you sell an inherited house?
sections.html:
Many Warren sales start with an estate. Under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30, an heir who has not lived in the house during the past year is excused from the state disclosure form, and so is a fiduciary selling for an estate, guardianship or trust. Other sellers of one-to-four unit homes must hand over the signed form.

Even then, buyers ask about known defects, so answer in writing and keep a copy.

sections.h2: How do Warren's roads and winters affect showing a house?
sections.html: A freeway carrying Ohio 82 bypasses the city, and Ohio 5 leads southwest to the Ohio Turnpike. US 422 and Ohio 45 also run through Warren. NOAA normals reproduced for the city list 40.81 inches of precipitation and 27.9 inches of snow per year, with 21 snowy days and a January mean minimum of 16.8 degrees. Plan showings around plowed walks, working heat and visible roof and gutter condition, since buyers check these first in winter.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a rental house in Warren?
faqs.a: Selling takes no separate permit, but the dwelling permit in section 1367.10 does not transfer. The buyer applies for a new one, and the Water Department wants proof of it before opening service.

faqs.q: What if I move out and list the house myself?
faqs.a: An empty house offered for sale by its owner counts as vacant under Chapter 1338 and must be registered within 30 days. A broker-listed house gets a six-month pass from the start of the listing.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to dispute my property value in Trumbull County?
faqs.a: By the end of March after the tax year, or the first-half collection date when that is later. The window for tax year 2025 closed March 31, 2026. Call the Auditor at 330-675-2420.

faqs.q: Does an inherited house need the Ohio disclosure form?
faqs.a: Usually not. Section 5302.30 excuses an heir who has not lived in the house for a year and also excuses fiduciaries acting for an estate.

faqs.q: Can I keep my homestead exemption after I sell?
faqs.a: No. The exemption belongs to the home you own and live in on January 1, so it ends with the sale. Your next home needs its own application with the county auditor.
